bugs.what: The PRISMFALL logo was clipped by the title card: the last letters ran off the edge at 1366x768.
bugs.fix: Smaller clamp() font size, tighter letter-spacing and white-space: nowrap.

bugs.what: The Prism meter track overlapped the right border of the well.
bugs.fix: Moved the meter 0.36 cells clear of the well and the Next panel 0.95 cells out.

bugs.what: Simultaneous callouts drew on top of each other and were unreadable (e.g. 'FEVER x2' over 'SINGLE').
bugs.fix: Callouts now take free vertical lanes: a new text steps below any active text it would overlap. First fix was incomplete (older callouts drift upward); lanes now use each callout's current position.

bugs.what: The first-run tutorial hint bar covered the bottom row of the well on 768 px tall screens.
bugs.fix: The hint sits under the well when there is room, otherwise in the empty upper well.

bugs.found: Code review before playtest; then a dedicated test
bugs.what: Mashing Space or Enter at the moment of game over could press 'Play again' and skip the results screen (lost feedback, accidental restart).
bugs.fix: Results buttons ignore input for 700 ms after appearing; other screens for 120 ms.

bugs.what: Opening Controls from the Pause menu hid the paused board behind the attract animation.
bugs.fix: The board renders whenever a run is paused, whichever menu is open.

bugs.what: The results screen was silent because the music stopped at game over and never resumed.
bugs.fix: The results screen starts the menu music.

bugs.what: The bottom row of the app icon spilled outside its rounded card.
bugs.fix: Re-laid out the icon tiles inside the card and re-exported all icon sizes.

bugs.found: Launcher test (curl + Playwright against the Linux build)
bugs.what: Prismfall.exe opened /index.html?launcher=1. Go's file server redirects that to / and drops the query, so the heartbeat never started and the launcher would stop serving 3 minutes into play (a reload would then fail).
bugs.fix: The launcher opens /?launcher=1 directly. Verified: HTTP 200, game boots, heartbeat pings arrive.

bugs.found: Visual re-test of B3 (scripted burst right after a clear)
bugs.what: Prism Burst or Hold pressed during the 0.3 s line-clear animation was silently ignored. It felt like a dropped input exactly when players reach for Burst.
bugs.fix: Burst and Hold pressed mid-clear are buffered and applied as soon as the clear finishes. A regression check was added to the harness.

bugs.what: At machine speed (~6.7 pieces/s) the bot cleared ~260 lines and reached 20G in Daily Bloom. It topped out at 1:38 instead of reaching the 3:00 limit. The game behaved correctly; the test expectation was wrong.
bugs.fix: Test change only: Runs 1 and 3 now pace the bot at human speed, which also makes the first-60-seconds observation realistic.

bugs.what: Four failures in the first passes came from the test script (navigation from a non-title screen, a run cap that stopped before game over, a Second Wind test that kept dropping after the rescue, and not waiting for the game-over animation).
bugs.fix: Harness fixed (toTitle helper, higher caps, stop at rescue). No game code changed for these.

known.text: All testing ran on Linux in headless Chromium. Assumption: Edge/Chrome on Windows behave the same, since the game uses standard canvas, Web Audio and localStorage only. Fonts will differ (Segoe UI on Windows vs DejaVu in these screenshots).
Not executed (no Windows here). It's a two-line script: start "" "%~dp0index.html". Assumption: it opens the default browser on Windows 10/11.

Cross-compiled for Windows x64 (PE32+ GUI, icon embedded). The same Go source was run as a Linux build and verified to serve the game, answer heartbeats and exit cleanly when a second copy starts. The .exe itself was never run on Windows. It isn't code-signed, so SmartScreen may warn.
Browsers store progress per address, so the .bat/index.html (file://) and the .exe (http://127.0.0.1:47613) keep separate progress. This is documented in README.txt.

Verified programmatically: the engine starts on the first click or key, all 22 SFX and both music modes run with no errors, and the sequencer advances. Assumption: the mix sounds good. It was never listened to; a headless browser has no speakers.
Tested with a mocked standard-mapping pad (navigator.getGamepads override), not a physical controller. Assumption: Xbox and PlayStation pads using the standard mapping behave the same.
Measured in headless Chromium with software rendering. Assumption: a desktop GPU is at least as smooth. Not measured on your machine.
The first-60-seconds judgement is my own assessment from watching bot runs and screenshots. No human has played it yet. Balance values (gem rate, perk costs, Burst size) are first-pass estimates.
The bot never uses T-spins and plays at machine precision. T-spin scoring was verified with a scripted setup instead (T-spin double = 1200).
All art is procedural placeholder art because SpriteCook wasn't connected. The full list of missing assets is in docs/ASSET_MANIFEST.md.
Not available. The playtest used Playwright + headless Chromium instead (real input events, real browser engine).
